summary.text: 这 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 這, now read zhè and used for “this” or “here.” Evidence for the traditional graph also records a separate older verb use meaning “meet” or “receive”; it does not establish that verb as the demonstrative’s source.

formation.text: For the traditional graph 這, an analysis of its older “meet/receive” verb use treats 辶 as semantic and 言 as phonetic. A Warring States manuscript graph containing 酉、口、言 has separately been proposed as 這 in that verb sense. Neither account establishes the formation of the later demonstrative or proves that these components belong to simplified 这. The formation of 这 is therefore derived: it is the simplified counterpart of 這, whose distinct internal construction cannot be assigned to this graph from the supplied evidence.

history.text: The supplied evidence identifies 这 as the simplified counterpart of 這, but does not date its standardization or document the graphic steps by which the form arose. No character-specific historical glyph sequence is available here.

For the traditional graph, a Warring States manuscript reading as the older verb “meet/receive” has been proposed. Accounts also report that 這 is absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and from Shuowen; this does not establish the oldest graph or a continuous graphic history.

uncertainties.text: The origin of the demonstrative “this/here” is unresolved. Proposals involve 者, 之, and a relation to 遮; reported Tang spellings and a proposed handwriting confusion with 遮 do not establish which account is correct.

The older verb “meet/receive” and the demonstrative are documented separately, with no demonstrated semantic bridge or proof that the demonstrative borrowed the graph from the verb. The reported Tang examples were not independently checked against their underlying dated texts.

The sound role assigned to 言 in analyses of traditional 這 lacks an independently verified ancient pronunciation comparison in this dossier. Current zhè readings for 這 and 这 do not establish that historical relation.

senses.text: The proximal demonstrative use is reported in Tang material, including the expression 這回. This is the earliest attested period reported here, not proof of the word’s original meaning.
The character is used as a proximal demonstrative referring to a nearby place as well as a thing; the supplied evidence does not establish a separate chronology for this use.

senses.period: Warring States manuscript proposal; exact attestation unresolved
senses.text: A manuscript graph has been proposed as 這 used for a verb meaning “meet” or “receive.” This is a distinct older lexical use; the evidence does not show it developed into the demonstrative.
A reported Yuan drama example uses 這 as an empty metrical filler. The evidence does not establish how this function relates to the demonstrative.

limitations.text: The reported Tang demonstrative examples establish an attested use, not its source. Competing proposals are insufficient to connect the demonstrative to the older verb or to another proposed source.
The evidence does not establish a semantic development from the demonstrative to the Yuan metrical filler.

overview.text: 这 is the simplified form of 這 and means “this” or “here.” The traditional graph also had a separate older verb use, “meet/receive”; no evidence here connects that verb to the demonstrative.

relationships.text: 这 is identified as the standardized simplified counterpart of 這. The evidence does not date the standardization process.
